title: Chicken Piccata
description: Flour-dusted chicken cutlets pan-fried in butter and finished in a bracing lemon-caper sauce. The kind of 30-minute dinner that punches well above its weight.

ingredients.name: boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.notes: butterflied and halved into 4 cutlets, pounded to 1/4-inch thick

steps.text: Season the chicken cutlets generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Spread the flour on a plate and dredge each cutlet, shaking off the excess.

Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. When the butter foams, add 2 cutlets and cook until golden, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
steps.tip: Don't crowd the pan — the cutlets need space to brown, not steam.

steps.text: Add 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter to the skillet. Sear the remaining 2 cutlets the same way, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer to the plate with the first batch.
Remove the pan from heat. Add the lemon juice, chicken stock, and capers. Return to the stove, bring to a boil, and scrape up the fond from the bottom of the pan. Season to taste.
steps.tip: The fond — those brown bits stuck to the pan — is where most of the flavor lives.

steps.text: Return all the chicken to the pan and simmer gently until warmed through and the sauce thickens slightly, about 5 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a serving platter. Whisk the remaining 2 tablespoons butter into the sauce until glossy and emulsified. Pour the sauce over the chicken and scatter the parsley on top.
